:::{#prp-complement-partition}
#### An event and its complement partition the sample space

For any [event](#def-event) $A$,
the events $A$ and its [complement](#def-complement) $\neg A$
are a [partition](#def-partition) of the [sample space](#def-sample-space) $\samplespace$.

:::

::: proof

The sample space $\samplespace$ is an event (@lem-sample-space-event),
so a partition of it is defined.
The complement $\neg A$ is the [set difference](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/sets.html#def-set-difference) $\setdiff{\samplespace}{A}$,
which is an event
because the events are closed under complements in $\samplespace$,
by the complement requirement of a
[$\sigma$-algebra](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures.html#def-sigma-algebra).
The events $A$ and $\neg A$ are mutually exclusive,
because $\neg A$ contains only elements not in $A$.
Their union is $\samplespace$,
because each element of $\samplespace$ is either in $A$ or not in $A$.

:::
